numbers.source: 1200 mm: the research note and the scene's earlier skip give about 1.2 m; it also fixes P1's scale (the skip's height from its top edge row 197.5 to its foot row 331.5 = 134 px, 0.1117 px per mm); error 100

numbers.what: widest length (at the junction of the two trapezia)
numbers.source: P1 tip_left_x 559.6 to tip_right_x 896.4 = 336.7 px at 0.1117 px per mm (the height is the assumed unit); error 150
P1 bottom_left_x 624.8 from the centre 728.0 = 924 mm half length (the right corner is faint; symmetry assumed); error 120
P1 rim_under_y 207.1 below the top edge 197.5: 9.6 px = 86 mm; error 20

numbers.what: stiffening rib centre above the floor
numbers.source: P1 rim_line_y 228.4 above the foot 331.5: 103.1 px = 923 mm; error 40
P1 tips at row 243 of the turned copy: (331.5 - 243) / 0.1117 = 792; error 50

numbers.what: width across the skip (the floor plus the side plates)
numbers.source: a 6-yard builder's skip is about 1.7 m wide over its side plates; the photograph is a side view and gives none; error 150

photos.method: the photograph is turned 7.2 degrees about (730, 270) because the skip stands tilted on a slope (the top rim's slope), then each edge is the strongest grey-level step inside the recorded window on the turned copy; the scale is fitted on the one span from the rim bar's lower edge to the foot (124.4 px for 1114 mm if the skip is 1200 high: 0.1117 px per mm); the height of 1200 is Judgement (it sets the scale), so the proportions are checked and the absolute lengths are judged; the right bottom corner and the top corners are against fence wire and sky and faint, so they are not used; the tolerance is the measured spread times 3 plus 2 px, at least 6 px (54 mm)

sources.author: Ian Taylor
sources.shows: a yellow builder's skip standing tilted on a grass slope, seen from its long side: the hexagonal side profile (two stacked trapezia, widest at about two thirds up), a folded top rim, a stiffening rib below it, two lifting lugs near the top, a stencilled firm's name and telephone number; behind it a temporary fence panel; two walkers and a dog on the left (outside the crop)
sources.not_used_for: absolute size (no scale object; the height 1200 is assumed), the firm's name and number (painted out), the people, the fence
sources.period: 2021; the builder's skip's shape has not changed since the 1960s (cantilever-lorry skips)

sources.author: Rossographer
sources.shows: a yellow skip from its end in a terraced street at the kerb: the end plates slope inward, a painted FILL LEVEL line below the rim, a telephone number, traffic cones at the end
sources.not_used_for: any number (oblique, with a number and a house for sale in the frame); the number and the street (not previewed)

owed.line: Put the skip back in the road before the yard, with its two lamps lit at night and a made-up hire firm's name on it, now that it is a real skip?

night.note: a skip in the highway carries two battery lamps (amber) at its ends; they glow in the lantern colour (1.0, 0.25, 0.0) linear, emissive 4 on a 90 mm lens; the yellow paint under the lantern reads orange-brown and the dents catch the glow

text.stencil: stencilled capitals on the side plate between z 450 and 760, black, name 120 mm tall, number 90 mm tall, centred; a second line 'FILL LEVEL' 40 mm tall painted on the end plates 120 below the rim
text.note: invented hire firm and an invented number (the 555 exchange); no real firm; the stencil is a texture; the name sits on the side facing the road and again on the other side; none on the ends but FILL LEVEL

placement.slot: west carriageway, the long side parallel to the kerb, centre x 22.5 m (in front of the yard mouth, x 21 to 24), 0.30 m from the kerb face (the skip's near side at z -2.70), the name on the road side; the two scene cones belong at the ends, 0.3 m beyond the skip
reasons: the 2 October ruling took the skip off the street 'until real'; the scene's story ('the yard is shut': a barrier across the mouth, cones, a skip) places it before the yard mouth, one event with the pallets behind the barrier (the pallets target)

the near lane is 3.0 m: a skip 1700 mm wide at 0.30 m from the kerb leaves 3.0 - 0.30 - 1.70 = 1.0 m in its own lane and the whole 3.0 m other lane: the street stays passable (2.8 m is the least a bus needs; cars are off in any case)
its length is 3.0 m, the width of the yard mouth: it fills the street frontage of the gap without crossing a shop front
the scene's two cones (x 21.3 and 23.7 at 0.35 m from the kerb) now stand inside the skip's length: they move to x 20.7 and 24.3 (a change for the scene's owner, not edited here)

a skip on the highway needs lamps at night and a permit: the two amber lamps are on the skip; the double yellow lines (0.25 m from the kerb) lie under it: a skip on the lines is a street fact (a permit, Judgement)

wear: yellow paint chalked, dented along the rim and the lower plates (a hundred dents 20 to 80 mm, seeds), chipped to rust at the rim's top edge and the lugs, rust runs 30 to 120 mm below the chipped places
mud and cement to knee height (a mask from the floor up, 0.4 m on the side plates), black tar and bitumen splashes, lime-white splashes
the stencilled name worn, a few letters chipped; the paint on the end plates scraped by the lorry's chains
the lamps: dirty lenses, one cracked (a seed)
contents: empty in the sample (a variant carries a heap of plasterboard, bricks and timber lath, never a person or a drink container: a seed in the builder's decals)
NOT shown: a real firm's name or number, a person, any drink container

variants_note: SK1 (the sample): the 6-yard skip, yellow, empty, on the road at the yard mouth.
colours: yellow (the sample), orange, blue-green; each firm paints all its skips one colour.
SK2 (not written as geometry): the 4-yard skip is SK1 scaled by 0.8 in x and y and 0.85 in z; its lugs move with it.
contents (seeds, never a mesh in the target): empty; half full of rubble; full with a heap above the rim. Nothing else.
not_settled: absolute size: S1 has no scale object, the height 1200 is assumed and sets 0.1117 px per mm; the profile's proportions are measured, its lengths follow
the width across (1700, Judgement: no end view was measured; S2's end view is oblique)
the right bottom corner and the top corners (faint against fence and sky in S1): the profile is taken symmetric about the centre of the widest line
whether a skip stood on Quay Street in 1990 (the scene's story says one did; the ruling put it back as soon as it is real)
the lamps' exact fixing (a hook over the rim: Judgement)
content_rule_note: no firm's real name, no person, no drink container in the contents (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: build by script: the two side plates are prisms of the hexagonal profile in the x-z plane (5 mm), the floor and the four end plates are boxes (the end plates' rotations are in target.json), the rim a folded bar along the top edge
texture: yellow paint with the stencil (TIDEWAY SKIP HIRE, TEL 555 0142) on the side plate; no real mark
lamps: emissive amber (1.0, 0.25, 0.0) linear at night, off by day; the lens 90 across
keep the hexagonal profile exact: its widest line is at 793 and its bottom edge shorter than its top
